title: Soba Noodle Bowl with Ginger-Mushroom Broth
cScaleSummary: C0 because the recipe contains no cholesterol-contributing animal-derived ingredients. The soba noodles, vegetable stock, kombu, mushrooms, tofu, bok choy, aromatics, soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, scallions, sesame seeds, and cilantro contribute 0 mg cholesterol.
ldlActiveSummary: LDL-Active because the recipe is built around soba, tofu, mushrooms, bok choy, kombu, and unsaturated oils, with fiber-rich plant ingredients and flavor developed through infusion, browning, aromatics, and careful finishing rather than saturated fat or cholesterol-containing ingredients.
intro: Soba has deep roots in Japanese cooking, where buckwheat noodles are served hot in broth, cold with dipping sauce, or simply dressed with a few precise seasonings. A good soba bowl does not need heaviness to feel complete. The pleasure comes from clean broth, springy noodles, mushrooms, greens, and a sharp aromatic lift from ginger and scallions.
miseEnPlace: Prepare {{ingredient:firm-tofu}} as specified: pressed and cut into 1/2-inch cubes.
Prepare {{ingredient:baby-bok-choy}} as specified: stems and leaves separated, chopped.

stepGroups.title: Make the Broth
items: Combine the kombu ({{quantity:kombu}}), dried shiitake mushrooms ({{quantity:dried-shiitake-mushrooms}}), and vegetable stock ({{quantity:vegetable-stock}}) in a pot.
Bring just to a bare simmer over medium heat. Remove the kombu before the stock boils.
Slice about half of the softened kombu into thin strips and return it to the stock. Discard the remaining kombu.
Turn off the heat and let the dried shiitakes steep in the hot stock for 15 minutes.
Remove the dried shiitakes, slice them thinly, and return them to the stock.
Heat the neutral oil ({{quantity:neutral-oil-broth}}) in a wide pot over medium-high heat.

Add the fresh mushrooms ({{quantity:fresh-mushrooms}}) and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they release their liquid, the liquid evaporates, and the mushrooms brown at the edges.
Add the garlic ({{quantity:garlic}}) and fresh ginger ({{quantity:fresh-ginger}}). Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the infused stock with sliced shiitakes, low-sodium soy sauce ({{quantity:soy-sauce-broth}}), rice vinegar ({{quantity:rice-vinegar}}), and black pepper ({{quantity:black-pepper}}).
Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
Turn off the heat and stir in the toasted sesame oil ({{quantity:toasted-sesame-oil}}).

stepGroups.title: Sear the Tofu
items: Pat the firm tofu ({{quantity:firm-tofu}}) dry.
Heat the neutral oil ({{quantity:neutral-oil-tofu}}) in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the tofu and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, turning occasionally, until lightly browned on several sides.
Add the low-sodium soy sauce ({{quantity:soy-sauce-tofu}}) and toss for 30 seconds, until the tofu is glazed and the pan is nearly dry.

stepGroups.title: Prepare the Noodles and Bowl
items: Cook the soba noodles ({{quantity:soba-noodles}}) according to the package directions.
Drain and rinse the noodles thoroughly under cool water to remove excess starch.
Briefly dip the rinsed noodles back into hot water for 20 to 30 seconds to rewarm, then drain again.
Add the chopped bok choy stems from the baby bok choy ({{quantity:baby-bok-choy}}) to the simmering broth and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the chopped bok choy leaves and cook for 30 to 60 seconds, until just wilted.
Divide the soba noodles among 4 bowls.
Ladle the hot broth, mushrooms, bok choy, and shiitakes over the noodles.
Add the seared tofu.
Finish with the scallions ({{quantity:scallions}}), toasted sesame seeds ({{quantity:toasted-sesame-seeds}}), and fresh cilantro ({{quantity:fresh-cilantro}}).
Serve hot.
